newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shares close higher in active trading.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shares close higher in active trading.

text.p: Israeli shares closed higher on Wednesday in active trading as investors responded favourably to the signing of the Hebron deal and to the IMF's upgrading of Israel to an industrialised economy, traders said.
The benchmark Mishtanim index of the top 100 shares gained 1.51 percent, or 3.53 points, to 237.33 on all-share turnover of 200 million shekels against 172 million shekels on Tuesday.
The Maof 25 blue chip index closed 1.42 percent higher at 245.04.

"The market reacted today to very good news: the rise of Israeli shares traded in New York, the Hebron deal and most important -- the upgrading of Israel to an industrialised economy," said Baruch Glicksberg of Clal Insurance.
Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Palestinian leader Yasser Arafat on Wednesday sealed a long-elusive deal to launch Palestinian self-rule in 80 percent of the West Bank town of Hebron.
On Tuesday the Bank of Israel said the International Monetary Fund (IMF) would from April classify Israel as an industrialised country.
"The IMF's decision will improve Israel's (credit) rating and attract more foreign investors to the local market," Glicksberg said.
"After Tuesday's correction the market can resume its rise. The positive momentum should continue on Thursday despite expectations for some profit-taking," said Yosi Weidelfeld at Eyal Securities.
After the end of trading, the Central Bureau of Statistics reported that the consumer price index rose 0.8 percent in December, which was at the high end of expectations.

Weidelfeld said before the release of the index: "The market expects a CPI figure of around 0.7 percent. A lower figure would send the market upwards. A CPI of 0.9 percent or more would be very dissappointing and will have a negative impact on trading."

Koor Industries, the most active share of the day, rose 3.0 percent to 32,493 agorot on volume of 5.4 million shekels. Koor said on Wednesday that Canada's Consumers Packaging Inc (CPI) would acquire 25.1 percent of Koor's Israel's Phoenicia Glass Works Ltd subsidiary as part of a strategic alliance.

Other active shares included Leumi Insurance Holdings, which surged 3.75 percent to 239 agorot on volume of 12.4 million shekels, and Teva Pharmaceutical Industries, which rose 3.5 percent to 1,775 agorot on turnover of 10 million shekels.

Teva said on Wednesday it would ask shareholders to approve a plan to exchange their par 0.01 shares for 0.1 shares on a 10-to-one basis. They will also be asked to approve doubling registered share capital by 100 million 0.1 shares.
